feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: single-column ELM (optionally coupled to PFLOTRAN) can simulate soil-column nitrogen cycling, leaching flux, and vertical nitrate transport to the water table, but it CANNOT resolve lateral groundwater transport, well capture zones, or well-specific arrival concentrations without a 3D groundwater flow-and-transport model.
answerable: Vertical soil water and nitrate leaching flux below the root zone under fertilized cropland
Soil column N cycling: nitrification, denitrification, plant uptake, mineralization
Nitrate concentration in soil pore water and recharge reaching the water table
Sensitivity of leaching to soil texture, fertilizer timing/rate, and climate forcing
not_answerable: Lateral advective-dispersive transport from field to a specific drinking-water well
Well capture-zone delineation and travel-time to individual wells
Arrival concentrations AT wells (requires 3D saturated-zone flow & transport, e.g., PFLOTRAN 3D or MODFLOW-MT3D)
Mixing/dilution in the regional aquifer and preferential flow through tile drains at basin scale

parsed.n_justification: Three columns span the dominant agricultural soil textures and landscape positions of the Upper Iowa basin (well-drained upland silt loam, poorly-drained loam lowland with tile drainage tendency, and coarser floodplain sandy loam) to bracket the range of nitrate leaching behavior driving recharge nitrate concentrations.
requires_capabilities: ELM-CN/BGC nitrogen cycle with prognostic NO3 pool (converging trophic cascade or nitrification-denitrification module)
Fertilizer application via crop management (prescribed FERT stream or dynamic crop model)
Vertically-resolved soil biogeochemistry (soil layer nitrate leaching)
PFLOTRAN coupling (ELM-PFLOTRAN interface) for finer vertical reactive nitrate transport to water table
Tile-drainage / lateral subsurface drainage parameterization for Corn Belt Mollisols
assumptions: Well arrival concentrations require a downstream 3D saturated-zone transport model; ELM/PFLOTRAN single-column output (recharge nitrate flux & concentration) is delivered as the source-term boundary condition to that model.
GSWP3/CRUNCEP-style atmospheric forcing at ~0.5 deg used for the single-column runs; 2001-2020 chosen to represent recent climate and land management.
Continuous corn/soybean rotation assumed as dominant land use with typical Midwest N fertilizer rates (~150-200 kg N/ha) applied in spring.
Atmospheric N deposition prescribed from a present-day dataset.
First 2-5 years treated as spin-up for soil moisture and N pools; analysis focuses on quasi-equilibrium later years.
Soil textures assigned per column approximate SSURGO-dominant series for the Upper Iowa basin.
